title: Score the frozen ORN-to-PN candidates once against the sealed wild-type trains, as a discrimination experiment
status: PREREGISTERED. Every criterion and every predicted number below was written before any train array was opened.

why_this_exists.the_position: Two candidate families are frozen from a fit to spent paired-pulse data. Their registered holdout returned NO VERDICT because its primary cohort turned out to be the training set, and the one genuine unseen cohort could not separate them. The trains are the only unspent wild-type ORN-to-PN holdout left in the corpus.
why_this_exists.what_makes_it_worth_the_last_holdout: It is a different observable, not another cohort, and it attacks precisely what the paired-pulse curve could not constrain. The paired-pulse protocol cannot measure the resource recovery constant at all -- every family drove it to its bound -- and a 1 Hz train of 32 pulses measures it directly: the candidates predict steady states of 0.341 and 0.402 there against the refuted v0.1 rule's 0.904. The candidates also differ from each other by up to 0.55 in normalised amplitude at 60 Hz, against 0.075 at their widest on a paired-pulse curve.
why_this_exists.it_is_a_discrimination_experiment_first: The primary question is which of the two frozen accounts survives, not whether either is right in absolute terms. Both questions are scored, and the discrimination one carries the verdict, because that is the question the fit set demonstrably could not answer and this observable demonstrably can.

byte_level.method: flysim.reservations.duplicate_arrays, which digests the stored element bytes of named arrays without decompressing or decoding any payload
byte_level.result: All 24 arrays in Fig3E_and_F.mat are stored distinctly from one another, and its 1 Hz arrays are distinct from Fig3B.mat's despite sharing both variable names. No train array duplicates anything already spent.
byte_level.what_this_settles_and_what_it_does_not: It settles that the trains are not a re-shipped copy of a spent array, which is the failure that voided the last holdout. It does not settle whether the same animals were recorded.

published_animal_counts.reading: Different counts, so the two sets are not identical. Not disjoint either, on any evidence available here.

subject_independence_audit.the_methods_sentence_that_decides_the_cl: 'Paired-pulse recordings were made at 0.2 Hz ... Ten seconds of rest were afforded to the cell in between recordings.' Rest afforded to *the cell* between recordings says that several protocols were run in one cell. So overlap between the train animals and the paired-pulse animals is not merely possible, it is what the methods describe.
subject_independence_audit.why_not_biological_independent: The methods describe multiple protocols per cell and the counts are compatible with the 17 train animals being a subset of the 20-to-22 paired-pulse animals. Nothing in the repository carries an animal identifier, so this cannot be resolved from what is staged.
subject_independence_audit.why_not_protocol_only: The counts differ, so the sets are not identical, and the trains are certainly a different observable measured under a different stimulation protocol. Calling it protocol-only would overstate the dependence as badly as calling it independent would understate it.

consequences_declared_now_for_each_class.if_biological_independent: Full weight. A pass would be a cross-observable validation on unseen animals and would support a V1 tier naming the observable.
consequences_declared_now_for_each_class.if_unknown_overlap_which_is_the_recorded: The asymmetry is declared in advance and is not symmetric. A FAILURE is stronger than usual: if the same cells that produced the fitted paired-pulse curve also produced these trains, then a model fitted to the first and failing the second is failing within the same cells, with no cohort variation available as an excuse. A PASS is weaker than usual: shared animals mean it may demonstrate within-cell consistency rather than generalisation across animals. A pass under this classification is therefore capped at V1-limited and must be reported with the word 'unknown-overlap' attached.
consequences_declared_now_for_each_class.if_protocol_only: Discrimination between the candidates stays valid, because that comparison is internal to the same data. Absolute validation would not be claimable at all.

the_data.everything_else_in_the_file_stays_sealed: The four RNAi train arrays, and all sixteen latency and jitter arrays. The candidates have no parameter for a cac knockdown and generate neither a latency nor a jitter, so opening any of them would spend a holdout this contract cannot score.
the_data.the_animal_count_discrepancy_to_reconcil: Every array is 18 rows while the published legend gives wt n = 17. The most likely explanation is a NaN-padded row, which the authors' own use of nanmean is consistent with. The run must report the number of all-NaN rows per array, and if the finite-row count is not 17 the discrepancy is recorded as an open question rather than explained away.

observation_model.the_arrays_are_absolute_currents: Fig3B's plotting code takes abs() of these values and labels the axis in pA, so the trains are absolute evoked currents and are presumably negative. The run takes absolute values before normalising.
observation_model.normalisation_primary: The cohort-mean trajectory divided by the cohort-mean first pulse. The mean across animals is formed first, at each pulse index, and the whole mean trajectory is then divided by its own first element.
observation_model.normalisation_secondary_reported_not_sco: The mean across animals of each animal's own trajectory divided by that animal's own first pulse.
observation_model.why_the_primary_is_the_primary: Dividing each animal's trajectory by its own first pulse divides by a single noisy measurement, which biases the ratio upward by roughly the squared coefficient of variation of that first pulse and inflates the variance of every later point. Normalising the cohort mean avoids that bias at the cost of weighting animals by their absolute amplitude. Both are computed; the first carries the verdict; the difference between them is reported, because a large difference is itself evidence about how noisy the first pulse is.
observation_model.missing_data_rule: A non-finite entry excludes that animal from that pulse index only, and the count of exclusions per index is reported. An animal whose first pulse is non-finite is excluded from the secondary normalisation entirely and reported separately.

frozen_predictions.source: Copied from the frozen candidates in stage2-stp-developmental-holdout-v1, whose parameters came from the fit artifact below. No refit, no adjustment, no reselection.
frozen_predictions.the_scorer_must_rederive_them: Each trajectory below is recomputed from the parameters at scoring time and the run refuses to proceed if any value disagrees by more than 1e-9, which is how a change in the simulator between this commit and the score would be caught.

the_nulls.null_1_is_a_real_mechanism_not_a_horizon: ND-06 v0.1, the refuted depression-only rule at its registered utilisation of 0.22 and recovery constant of 893 ms. It is published, it is mechanistic, and on trains it is sharply different from both candidates: it never facilitates, its peak is always the first pulse, and its 1 Hz steady state is 0.904 against the candidates' 0.341 and 0.402. Requiring a candidate to beat it is a real bar.
the_nulls.why_this_matters_here: The previous holdout's null was a frozen constant, and the resulting margin was reported as a factor of 26 when the cohort means spanned 0.92 to 1.46, so any roughly-right shape would have beaten it. That overstatement is on the record. Using the refuted predecessor as the null removes the objection: a candidate that beats v0.1 on trains has beaten the best previously registered account of this synapse.
the_nulls.null_2_flat: A constant at 1.0, reported for reference and carrying no criterion.
the_nulls.v0_1_is_not_on_trial_here: It is already refuted on the paired-pulse observable and nothing this contract returns can un-refute it. If it beats both candidates on trains that is recorded plainly as what it is: the candidates fail to improve on a rule that is known to be wrong elsewhere.

hypotheses.name: discrimination between the two frozen candidates
hypotheses.statement: Summed over the four frequencies, the weighted squared error of one candidate's frozen trajectory against the cohort-mean normalised trajectory is at most half the other's. The candidate meeting that is the winner.
hypotheses.weights: one over the squared standard error of the cohort mean at each pulse index
hypotheses.criterion: a ratio of summed weighted error, better over worse, of at most 0.5
hypotheses.degenerate_outcome_check: If the two frozen trajectories differ by less than the cohort standard error at every pulse of every frequency, this observable cannot separate them and R1 is NO VERDICT regardless of the error ratio. Computed before scoring: the frozen curves differ by up to 0.079 at 1 Hz, 0.096 at 10 Hz, 0.165 at 20 Hz and 0.551 at 60 Hz, so the check is expected to clear, and it is still evaluated against the measured standard errors rather than assumed.
hypotheses.if_neither_wins: Recorded as NOT SEPARATED. Neither candidate may then be preferred over the other on any evidence in this project.

hypotheses.name: the winner beats the refuted predecessor
hypotheses.statement: The R1 winner's summed weighted error is at most half that of ND-06 v0.1 on the same data under the same normalisation.
hypotheses.criterion: a ratio of summed weighted error, candidate over v0.1, of at most 0.5
hypotheses.why_both_R1_and_R2_are_primary: R1 alone could be won by the less bad of two bad accounts. R2 alone could be passed by a candidate that beats a rule already known to be wrong without describing the data. The verdict requires both.
hypotheses.degenerate_outcome_check: If ND-06 v0.1's summed weighted error is itself below that of the flat null, it is a strong null and R2 is informative. If it is worse than the flat null, R2 is recorded as passed against a weak null and the verdict rests on R3.

hypotheses.name: the recovery constant, measured at last
hypotheses.statement: The 1 Hz steady state, taken as the mean of the last five normalised pulses, lies inside the winner's frozen prediction's bootstrap interval. The candidates predict 0.341 and 0.402; v0.1 predicts 0.904.
hypotheses.why_it_is_here: The paired-pulse protocol cannot measure the resource recovery constant at all: every family drove it to its bound because the 300 ms and 1000 ms cohort means differ by 0.0003. This is the observable that constrains it, and it is the single number this whole exercise most wants.
hypotheses.no_refit_permitted_on_it: Whatever this returns, no parameter may be adjusted under this contract or cited as evidence for an adjusted one.

hypotheses.name: early facilitation and where the peak sits
hypotheses.statement: The second-over-first ratio and the one-indexed peak pulse are reported at each frequency against both candidates' frozen values. The candidates disagree about the peak at 10 Hz (pulse 2 against pulse 1) and at 20 Hz (pulse 3 against pulse 2), and v0.1 predicts pulse 1 at every frequency.
hypotheses.why_it_has_no_criterion: Peak index is a discrete statistic on a noisy trajectory and a criterion on it would be dominated by the noise at the pulses either side. It is reported because it is the most legible way to see which account the data resemble.

expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.prediction: Both candidates are expected to over-predict facilitation at 20 and 60 Hz, because their facilitation was fitted to a paired-pulse curve whose shortest interval is 10 ms and neither has any mechanism that limits facilitation when spikes arrive every 17 ms. The 1 Hz steady state is the least certain and the most informative: it is a genuine extrapolation of a pinned constant.
expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.what_would_surprise_me: A clean R1 separation in favour of the four-parameter candidate. On the fit set the five-parameter one was better by a factor of hundreds; on the day-0 cohort the four-parameter one was marginally better. A decisive win for the simpler account would suggest the second facilitation timescale was fitting noise in the 30 ms cohort mean.
expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.why_this_is_written_down: So that a result matching the expectation cannot be presented afterwards as a stronger confirmation than it is, and so that a surprise is recognisable as one.

acceptance.verdict_rule: PASS if and only if R1 identifies a winner and R2 is passed by that winner. R3 and R4 are reported and do not enter the verdict.
acceptance.what_a_pass_would_establish: That one of two frozen accounts of this synapse, fitted to a different observable and frozen with every predicted number written down beforehand, describes evoked trains across four stimulation frequencies better than the refuted rule it replaces. Under the recorded UNKNOWN-OVERLAP classification that is worth a V1-limited tier on the ORN-to-PN train observable in one laboratory, and it must be reported with the overlap caveat attached.
acceptance.what_a_pass_would_not_establish: Nothing about another laboratory, another glomerulus, another synapse class, latencies, jitter, absolute amplitudes or any perturbation. Nothing about edge sign, which stays unresolved under ND-10. And nothing that resolves the release-probability incompatibility recorded in the candidate registry, which no train measurement can settle.
acceptance.what_a_failure_would_establish: Under UNKNOWN-OVERLAP a failure is the stronger outcome: if these are substantially the same cells that produced the fitted paired-pulse curve, then an account fitted to one observable in those cells fails another observable in the same cells, and the account is wrong rather than merely ungeneralised. The paired-pulse route to a dynamical tier for this synapse would then be closed and the next attempt would need a different class of model, not a different fit.
acceptance.no_refitting: No parameter may be changed on this outcome and no successor may cite this test as evidence for its own values.
acceptance.no_criterion_may_be_restated: R1's margin, R2's margin, the normalisation rule, the missing-data rule and all degenerate-outcome checks are closed as of this commit.
acceptance.scored_once: The four wild-type train arrays are opened once. The contract's values_opened flag is set on completion and the scorer refuses a contract that already records them as opened.

the_guard_that_must_run_first: flysim.reservations.duplicate_arrays against every array already spent -- Fig3D's five wild-type paired-pulse arrays, Fig3H's five, and Fig3B's 1 Hz control. The scorer refuses to open a cohort that duplicates a spent one before a byte of payload is decoded. This has already been run and is clean; it runs again at scoring time because the clean result is only as current as the run that produced it.
claim_boundary: One scoring pass over four sealed wild-type train arrays against models frozen beforehand, in a cohort whose overlap with the fitting cohort is unknown and declared unknown. It opens four arrays and leaves the RNAi trains, the latency and jitter arrays, and the whole Takagi corpus sealed. It can award at most a V1-limited tier and it cannot resolve the release-probability incompatibility.
